top_news.title: 3 killed, 36 injured in Houthi attacks on Abha, King Khalid airports: Saudi GACA
top_news.summary: Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport were targeted in two separate attacks on October 6 and 7, resulting in a total of three fatalities and 36 injuries, Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said. According to GACA, two people were killed and 28 injured in the attack on Abha International Airport. The deceased were female residents of Moroccan and Algerian nationalities, while the injured included Saudi citizens, a Bangladeshi resident and a Filipino resident. The injuries ranged from minor to critical. At King Khalid International Airport, one Sudanese resident was killed, and eight people were injured, GACA said. The injured included five Saudi citizens, two Egyptian residents and one Pakistani resident, with injuries ranging from minor to critical. All injured individuals were transported to hospital for appropriate medical care, GACA said, adding that the two attacks also caused some property damage. The authority said emergency response teams and relevant authorities responded immediately in accordance with established protocols and applicable emergency response plans.
